english.html: a Greek word which signifies what the Latins call PAGUS, that is to say a town and village, and ODE, which signifies song: which is as much as to say the song of the villages and villagers. For in the beginning the Greeks, when they wished to rebuke and tax the vices and evil life of certain persons, were wont to assemble through the villages and the crossroads of the towns, and there, singing, to publish the life of those whom they wished to objurgate and reprove. In this kind of fable and poetry, although the beginning was troublous and sad, the issue nevertheless was happy, pleasant and agreeable: as all the Comedies of Plautus and of Terence demonstrate. But in Tragedy there are represented, in a high and grave style, the manners, adversities and calamitous life of captains, Dukes, Kings and Princes; it having always been so called because the first prize that was proposed for the best players of this kind of poetry was a GOAT, which the Greeks call TRAGOS.
He who in tragic song competed for a paltry goat c (Carmine qui tragico, vilem, certauit ob hircum).

notes.original: Horace au liure de l'art poëtique.
notes.gloss: Carmine qui tragico vilem certavit ob hircum: the poet who first competed in tragic verse for a paltry he-goat — the etymology of tragedy from the goat given as the prize.

english.html: Or else a Goat's skin full of wine: and ODE, which signifies song — that is to say, Goat-song. And this kind of fable always has a sad, unhappy and lamentable issue: whence is now drawn and taken the manner of speaking, which many in this time use, of calling unhappy and unfortunate deeds (even though they are transacted among vile and abject persons) plays of tragedy.

And in order to attain it the more conveniently, he resolved to inquire and inform himself, as warily as he could, from the said Pujol, Quillet, and other familiar friends and neighbours, of the condition of the said Martin Guerre: of his father, wife, sisters, uncle and other kinsfolk; together with what the same Martin

lines: vocable Grec, qui ſignifie, ce q̃ les Latins appellent PA-
GVS: c'eſt à dire vn bourg & village: & ODE qui ſignifie
chant, qu'eſt autant à dire comme chant des villages, &
villageois. Car du commẽcement les Grecs, lors qu'ils
vouloyẽt increper & taxer les vices, & mauuaiſe vie de
quelques vns, ils ſouloyent ſ'aſſembler par les villages,
& carrefours des villes: & illec en chantant, publier la
vie de ceux qu'ils vouloyẽt obiurguer, & reprendre. En
cette eſpece de fable & poëſie, bien que le commence-
mẽt fuſt faſcheux, & triſte: l'iſſuë toutesfois eſtoit heu-
reuſe, plaiſante & aggreable: comme demonſtrent tou-
tes les Comedies de Plaute, & de Terence. Mais en la
Tragedie, ſont repreſentees par vn ſtyle haut, & graue,
les mœurs, aduerſitez, & vie calamiteuſe des capitai-
nes, Ducs, Roys, & Princes: ayant touſiours eſté ainſi
appellée, par ce que le premier prix qui fut propoſé
aux meilleurs iouëurs de cette eſpece de poëſie, fut vn
BOVC, que les Grecs nomment TRAGOS.
Carmine qui tragico, vilem, certauit ob
hircum {c}.
Ou bien vne peau de Bouc, pleine de vin: & ODE, qui
ſignifie chant, c'eſt à dire chant de Bouc. Et cette eſpece
de fable a touſiours l'iſſuë triſte, malheureuſe & lamen-
table: dont eſt ores tiree & priſe la maniere de parler:
de laquelle pluſieurs en ce temps vſent, d'appeller les
actes infelices & malheureux (bien que ſont traittez
entre perſonnes viles & abiectes) ieux de tragedie.
Et pour paruenir plus commodement
ſ'aduiſa de ſ'enquerir, & informer le plus
cautement qu'il pourroit, auec leſdits Pu-
iol, Quillet, & autres amis familiers, &
voiſins, de l'eſtat dud. Martin Guerre: de
ſes pere, femme, ſœurs, oncle, & autres pa
rens: enſemble de ce qu'iceluy Martin
